pages.source:
Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 24-Dec-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE MAKEUP EXAMINATIONS - DECEMBER 2025  
  Generative AI and Large Language Models [NPT_4121]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                     Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Design an evaluation framework to interpret and compare different word embedding models                 (5)  
  (e.g., Word2Vec, GloVe, FastText) using visualization techniques. Discuss how visualization  
  A)           helps in diagnosing embedding quality and bias.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Demonstrate how GPT (Generative Pre-trained Transformer) functions as a decoder-only                    (3)  
  model. Explain how its architecture enables tasks like text generation and completion.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)           Illustrate the role of the Encoder-Decoder model in sequence-to-sequence tasks such as                  (2)  
  language translation and show how this architecture enables a system to convert input sequences  
  into meaningful outputs.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2)                Evaluate the limitations of basic RNN architectures and justify how advanced types like LSTM and (5)  
  GRU overcome them. Compare their internal mechanisms and performance trade-offs in sequence  
  A)           learning tasks.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Apply the concept of ULMFiT to a sentiment classification task with limited labeled data. Explain       (3)  
  how each stage of fine-tuning helps improve model accuracy in this scenario.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)           Apply your understanding of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to describe two key factors that have driven   (2)  
  its rapid growth in recent years and demonstrate how each factor is reflected in real-world AI  
  applications.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3)                Analyze the implementation of a Generative AI system for automated news summarization                   (5)  
  using the Transformer architecture. Evaluate how each stage of the Generative AI Project  
  A)           Lifecycle contributes to ensuring accuracy, fairness, and ethical AI deployment.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  
  Page #1

B)         Evaluate one real-world application of Generative AI and analyze how representation learning            (3)  
  enables it to perform complex creative tasks.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)         Identify the phenomenon of hallucination in Large Language Models (LLMs) and illustrate how it          (2)  
  affects the reliability and trustworthiness of AI-generated outputs in real-world applications.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4)              Evaluate why Transformer-based Large Language Models (LLMs) have become the dominant                    (5)  
  architecture in modern AI. Justify your answer by analyzing their scalability, efficiency, and  
  A)         emergent capabilities compared to earlier models like RNNs or LSTMs.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)         Apply the concept of the Generative AI Project Lifecycle to describe how a company developing           (3)  
  an AI-based chatbot for customer support would structure its workflow from data collection to  
  deployment.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)         Apply your understanding of Natural Language Processing (NLP) to illustrate any two real-world          (2)  
  applications and explain how they create practical impact in solving everyday problems.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5)              Analyze the role of Instruction Tuning in improving the usability and reliability of large language     (5)  
  models. Discuss its effect compared to standard fine-tuning.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)         Apply your understanding of Cost Intuition and Risks to explain two major challenges faced when (3)  
  deploying LLMs at scale in production environments.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)         Apply your understanding of Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) architectures to classify the four           (2)  
  types of RNNs based on input-output cardinality, and illustrate each type with a suitable real-world  
  example.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  
  -----End-----
